laws.rule: In Dubrovnik's historic core, walking in swimwear, without clothing or partly clothed is prohibited under Article 95 of the city's municipal order decree. Communal wardens and police issue on-the-spot fines (1,000 kuna in 2022, about EUR 130).
laws.heading: Grad Dubrovnik, Odluka o komunalnom redu, art. 95

laws.rule: In Mljet National Park, camping, open fires, fishing, diving in Veliko and Malo jezero (the two lakes), walking in the woods at night, picking plants and disturbing animals are banned, and smoking is allowed only in designated places. A breach can be fined; the page lists no amounts.
laws.heading: Code of conduct, NP Mljet

laws.rule: Article 191 of Dubrovnik's communal order decision bans drinking alcohol on all public areas, except a licensed cafe or restaurant terrace on city land or an event approved by the city. This is the 2020 text as published in the city gazette; later amendments were not read.
laws.heading: Grad Dubrovnik, Odluka o komunalnom redu (Službeni glasnik br. 12, 18 September 2020)

laws.rule: Article 95 also bans, in the historic core (Grad, inside the walls): riding bicycles, electric scooters, motorbikes, mopeds and cars without approval (children under 7 on bicycles are the exception); dropping cigarette butts; spitting; walking dogs off the lead; eating, drinking and behaving improperly near cultural monuments; and climbing on the city walls or ignoring the posted rules. Article 61 also bans bathing in public fountains and taking out coins thrown into them. The gazette lists fines for businesses and people in kuna. On-the-spot payment is set at half the fine. No euro amount for individuals was read.
laws.heading: Grad Dubrovnik, Odluka o komunalnom redu (Službeni glasnik br. 12, 18 September 2020)

sources.title: Odluka o komunalnom redu (Službeni glasnik Grada Dubrovnika 12/2020)

layers.process: Mljet National Park needs a ticket (entry points Crna klada, Pomena, Polače). The 2026 adult ticket is EUR 20 from 1 January to 31 May and 1 October to 31 December, and EUR 30 from 1 June to 30 September (about A$31.78 and A$47.67 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293). Children 8 to 18 pay EUR 5 or 8; under 7 are free. The ticket includes one return solar-boat trip to St Mary's islet, inland sites, marked trails and parking at Vrbovica. A vessel ticket is separate: a vessel up to 6.99 m pays EUR 25 (EUR 20 on the webshop) from October to May and EUR 50 (EUR 40 on the webshop) from June to September, and does not cover the land sites or the Great and Small Lake.

Flying a drone in Mljet National Park needs the park's authorisation; commercial, promotional or research filming also needs details of who commissioned it and the project. The park publishes a drone permit application form.
